questions.q: As of which MySQL version did first-class roles become available?
options: MySQL 8.0
MySQL 5.5
MySQL 5.7
Roles have existed since MySQL's earliest versions
questions.explain: MySQL 8.0, released in 2018, introduced roles; before that, DBAs had to repeat GRANT statements per account.

questions.q: How are privileges assigned to a MySQL role?
options: Using the same GRANT syntax used for users, with the role in place of a user@host account
Roles cannot be granted privileges directly
Only through MySQL Workbench's GUI
By editing my.cnf directly
questions.explain: A role is implemented internally much like a user, so the standard GRANT ... TO 'rolename' syntax applies.

questions.q: If a role's privileges change after several users already hold that role, what happens to those users' effective privileges?
options: They update immediately for every account holding the role, with no additional GRANT statements needed
Each user must be re-granted the role manually for the change to apply
Only newly created accounts see the updated privileges
Role privilege changes require a server restart to take effect
questions.explain: This propagation is the core benefit of roles — manage the privilege set once, on the role, instead of per account.

questions.q: Does GRANT 'app_readonly' TO 'analyst_jane'@'10.0.5.%'; alone make the role active when analyst_jane connects?
options: No — without SET DEFAULT ROLE, the role is granted but not automatically active on connection
Yes, granting a role always makes it immediately active
Only if the role was created with the ACTIVE keyword
Roles are always active for every account that exists on the server
questions.explain: SET DEFAULT ROLE is required to make a granted role active automatically on every future connection; otherwise SET ROLE must be run manually each session.

questions.q: What does SET ROLE 'app_readonly'; do if a user has not been given a default role?
options: Manually activates the granted role for the current session only
Permanently sets the role as default for all future connections
Creates a new role named app_readonly
Removes the role from the account entirely
questions.explain: SET ROLE activates a granted role for the current session; it does not persist across new connections without SET DEFAULT ROLE.
